common_name: Mini Love Watermelon (Personal-Size Crack-Resistant AAS Winner)

planting.note: Start indoors or transplant after soil is thoroughly warm; Mini Love is a 2017 All-America Selections winner producing personal-size, 3-6 pound melons on more compact vines than standard watermelon, a good fit for small Gulf Coast gardens and trellising.

directions: Transplant into warm, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun once nights stay reliably warm; Mini Love is a personal-size seeded watermelon bred for early maturity and crack resistance, producing round, 3-6 pound fruit with sweet, crisp, deep red flesh perfect for a single small household to finish in one sitting. Its shorter vines and lighter fruit make it a good candidate for growing up a trellis with fruit slings for support, saving ground space in a small garden. Because it matures faster than standard full-size watermelon, it also fits well into a shorter spring or fall planting window. Harvest when the ground spot beneath the fruit turns from white to creamy yellow and the nearest tendril has dried and browned.
sources: All-America Selections — Mini Love watermelon AAS winner 2017

planting.note: Direct sow in fall for cool-season production, or in late winter for an early spring crop; Corvair carries resistance to numerous downy mildew races and is slow to bolt, making it a strong choice for the Gulf South's mild winter spinach window.

directions: Direct sow seeds 0.5 inch deep in moist, fertile, well-drained soil; thin to 2-4 inch spacing and use thinnings in salads. Corvair is a smooth-leaf hybrid spinach bred with resistance to numerous races of downy mildew, the fungal disease that most commonly cuts a spinach planting short in humid or damp conditions, and it holds an upright habit that keeps leaves cleaner and easier to harvest than sprawling types. Its slow-bolting habit extends the productive window into warmer weather better than many older varieties, useful for stretching a Gulf Coast spring or fall spinach crop. Harvest by cutting outer leaves for continued production or cutting the whole plant at the base once it has filled out.

common_name: Renegade Spinach (Downy Mildew and Mosaic Virus-Resistant Hybrid)

planting.note: Direct sow in fall for cool-season production, or in late winter for an early spring crop; Renegade carries resistance to numerous downy mildew races plus cucumber mosaic virus, and shows good bolt and cold tolerance suited to high-tunnel or open-garden winter production in the mild Gulf Coast climate.

directions: Direct sow seeds 0.5 inch deep in moist, fertile, well-drained soil; thin to 2-4 inch spacing and use thinnings in salads. Renegade is a spinach hybrid bred with resistance to numerous races of downy mildew along with tolerance to cucumber mosaic virus, giving it a broader disease package than most spinach varieties and helping it stay productive through the damp, changeable weather of a Gulf South winter. It also shows good bolt tolerance, holding a harvestable rosette longer into warming spring weather than many varieties. The upright, dark green leaves are well suited to both fresh eating and cooking. Harvest by cutting outer leaves for continued production or cutting the whole plant at the base once it has filled out.

planting.note: Direct sow in fall for cool-season production, or in late winter for an early spring crop; Acadia carries resistance to an unusually wide range of downy mildew races, a valuable trait for the damp, disease-prone conditions of a Gulf South winter spinach planting.

directions: Direct sow seeds 0.5 inch deep in moist, fertile, well-drained soil; thin to 2-4 inch spacing and use thinnings in salads. Acadia is a semi-savoy spinach hybrid, with leaves that carry moderate crinkle for good texture while staying easier to wash clean than fully savoy types, bred with resistance to an unusually wide range of downy mildew races that helps it stay healthy through the damp, humid conditions common in a Gulf South fall or winter garden. It is well suited to both field and high-tunnel production for a spring or fall crop. Harvest by cutting outer leaves for continued production or cutting the whole plant at the base once it has filled out, and use promptly since fresh spinach quality declines quickly after harvest.

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost when soil has warmed to at least 65 degrees; Serendipity was the original TripleSweet-type bicolor hybrid, blending sugary-enhanced tenderness with supersweet-level sugar content for excellent flavor and good holding quality.

directions: Sow seed 1 inch deep in warm soil, planting in blocks of several short rows rather than one long row to ensure good pollination; Serendipity is a widely grown bicolor sweet corn hybrid combining sugary-enhanced tenderness with the high sugar content and slower sugar-to-starch conversion typical of supersweet types, giving it both excellent eating quality and good holding time after picking. It produces large, well-filled ears with a mix of yellow and white kernels on tall, vigorous stalks. Feed with nitrogen and water deeply during tasseling and ear fill for the best-filled ears. Harvest when silks have browned and kernels are plump and release a milky juice when pressed.
sources: seed catalog reference (Rupp Seeds, Elk Mound Seed, Andrews Seed Company)
